metadata.title: What Is a Compression-Ring Fitting? Design, Sizes and Selection
metadata.seoTitle: What Is a Compression-Ring Fitting? Design, Sizes and Selection | FOREACH
metadata.seoDescription: Explore FOREACH HSF6 fittings and CL-1S/CL-1X kits: threads, tubing sizes, materials, assembly pliers, installation torque and pressure considerations.
metadata.coverAlt: FOREACH compression-ring fitting with tubing, stainless-steel ring and sealing ferrule

deck: A compression-ring fitting combines a threaded nut, a compression ring and a sealing ferrule without requiring a preformed tubing flange. Using FOREACH HSF6 and CL-1S as examples, this guide covers M6×1 and 1/4-28 UNF ports, tubing ODs from 1.6 to 3.2 mm, PPS/PEEK nuts, stainless-steel rings and PEEK ferrules, together with prefabrication, installation and reconnection.

leadBlocks.text: A compression-ring fitting is a flangeless threaded connection for instrument fluidics. It consists of a fitting nut, a compression ring and a sealing ferrule. After square-cutting the tubing, the matched ring and ferrule are preassembled on the end. The nut then loads this assembly against the receiving port to make the seal. Applications include reagent transfer, sample handling and wash lines linking tubing to pumps, valves and fluidic modules in analytical instruments and laboratory automation.

FOREACH HSF6 compact fittings are available with M6×1 and 1/4-28 UNF threads. The configurations covered here accept 1.6, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0 and 3.2 mm OD tubing. Nut materials include PPS and PEEK; the CL-1S kit combines a stainless-steel compression ring with a PEEK sealing ferrule. The illustrated HSF6 has a 6.0 mm head diameter and a 20.0 mm overall length. Use these dimensions to assess port spacing and axial clearance. Thread, tubing-size and material combinations are listed below.

These connections support on-site assembly and prefabricated tubing assemblies with specified lengths, end fittings and identification labels. Complete tubing ends can be disconnected and reconnected for maintenance as specified. This article focuses on HSF6/CL-1S and separately describes CL-1X-16 for smaller 6-40 UNF connections. Select other series and sizes against their own drawings.

sections.title: What is a compression-ring fitting? Nut, ring and ferrule

blocks.text: Here, compression-ring fitting means a microfluidic tubing connection using a separate compression ring and sealing ferrule. It is a type of flangeless connection. Flangeless means no preformed tubing flange is required; it does not imply that all such fittings use the same parts. The compression ring is not a circlip or snap ring used in a shaft groove.

blocks.text: In CL-1S, the compression ring is SUS stainless steel and the sealing ferrule is PEEK. The nut, ring and ferrule are separate components. A PEEK or PPS nut does not mean all wetted surfaces in the connection use that material.

sections.title: How does it seal, and why use prefabricated tubing?

blocks.text: As the nut screws into a flat-bottom receiving port, it transfers axial force to the ring and ferrule. Compression at the specified position brings the tubing-end assembly against the port sealing surface. Both ring-to-ferrule fit and tubing-end position matter. The thread provides retention and load; correct contact at the sealing interface must be checked.

blocks.title: Prepare the tubing end before connecting the instrument

blocks.text: Specify tubing, length, end components and labels before prefabrication. Completing the ends first supports batch assembly and line identification. During connection, the nut can rotate relative to the tubing, reducing twist caused by tightening. This is not a rotary union for continuous rotation during operation.

A serviceable complete tubing-end assembly can be retained during maintenance, but inspect the ferrule face, ring position and tubing condition. Reconnecting an intact end is different from removing an old ring and fitting it to new tubing.

sections.title: HSF6 threads, tubing sizes, materials and dimensions

blocks.text: HSF6 identifies the fitting nut series; CL-1S and CL-1X identify the ring-and-ferrule kits. Select the nut for the port, then the kit for the actual tubing OD. These three series are not interchangeable fitting models. The table covers the HSF6 configurations discussed here, not every compression-ring product.

blocks.title: One nut size can require several different tubing kits

blocks.text: For 2.5 mm OD tubing in an M6 flat-bottom port, start by checking HSF6-M6-32-PS-B with CL-1S-25. The code 32 identifies this nut size group. The kit must still be size 25 for 2.5 mm tubing; do not choose CL-1S-32 simply to match the nut code.

blocks.title: CL-1X-16 is a separate small-port configuration

blocks.alt: Black and natural-colored fittings showing metal rings, sealing ferrules and tubing-end positions
blocks.caption: Actual tubing-end assemblies showing the relative positions of the metal ring, sealing ferrule and tubing. Confirm model compatibility and dimensions against the applicable specifications.

blocks.text: CL-1X-16 accepts 1.6 mm OD tubing and uses a SUS ring with a PEEK ferrule. Its matching fitting is HFL6-U40-16 with a 6-40 UNF thread. Although it accepts the same tubing OD as CL-1S-16, the port, kit geometry and fitting differ; they are not directly interchangeable.

blocks.text: These dimensions describe the illustrated HSF6, not HSF, HFL6 or other configurations. The assembly must reach its sealing position while retaining adequate thread engagement. If the nut bottoms against the instrument surface before the ferrule seats, additional torque will not correct the dimensional mismatch.

sections.title: Choosing between compression-ring, ferrule and flanged fittings

blocks.text: Compare tubing-end preparation and sealing components first, then production assembly and maintenance. Compression-ring and conventional ferrule connections both avoid flanging. The former uses a separate ring and sealing ferrule; the latter uses a matched ferrule to grip the tubing and participate in sealing.

blocks.text: FOREACH assemblies can use FEP or PTFE tubing with specified lengths and labels. OD determines nut and kit compatibility; ID and length affect flow resistance and internal volume. Tubing with the same OD but different IDs can behave differently in flow and after pressing.

For selection, provide both port drawings, tubing ID/OD, finished length and measurement reference, fluid and cleaning conditions, temperature, continuous and peak pressures, and maintenance requirements. Select each end separately if the ports differ. O-rings or stop sleeves on the tubing limit nut travel; they are not the instrument-port seal.

blocks.title: Separate initial preassembly from connection to the port

blocks.text: Initial assembly requires the dedicated compatible pliers to press the compression ring and sealing ferrule into position. Hand pressure alone is unlikely to assemble them correctly. Tightening the nut or increasing port torque cannot replace preassembly. For maintenance reconnection, inspect the already assembled tubing end before inserting it into the port.

FOREACH assembly pliers are model T-SF-4-SS, product code 959016. When assembling tubing yourself, obtain the tool compatible with the kit and tubing size and confirm clamping position and operating instructions.

items: Cut the tubing square: use a suitable cutter, remove debris and check for flattening, burrs or cracks.
Check orientation: slide on the nut, ring and ferrule in order, following the selected kit diagram.
Position and preassemble: align the tubing end flush with the ferrule face, press with the dedicated compatible assembly pliers, then check ring seating and tubing recession or protrusion.
Connect the port: clean and inspect the sealing surface, hold the assembly in position and tighten as specified.
Check the connection: secure the tubing and test for leakage, air ingress and end movement at the specified fluid, temperature and pressure conditions.

blocks.title: What pressure can the fitting withstand?

blocks.text: Pressure capability applies to the complete nut, kit, tubing and port combination at stated temperatures and operating conditions. No common HSF6/CL-1S pressure rating is assigned here. Obtain the allowable working pressure for the selected combination. Check positive pressure, vacuum and start/stop peaks separately; a PEEK nut or metal ring alone does not establish pressure capability.

FOREACH plastic rigid-tubing fittings with M6×1 or 1/4-28 UNF threads have a recommended installation torque of 0.25–0.30 N·m. Plastic U40 compression-ring fittings with 6-40 UNF threads use 0.08–0.15 N·m. Match the recommendation to the thread and nut material.

These values apply to threaded tightening into the port, not the pressing force for kit preassembly. Preassemble the ring and ferrule correctly, tighten to the corresponding torque, then check sealing and tubing-end position.

blocks.text: Reconnection as specified does not mean unlimited cycles or maintenance-free use. For frequent disconnection, define test cycles, operating conditions and allowable leakage. Record sealing, tubing-end position and flow after each cycle. Address worn faces, cracks or ring movement according to the assembly requirements.

faqItems.question: Is a compression-ring fitting also flangeless?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The ring-and-ferrule design described here uses square-cut tubing without a preformed flange. Conventional ferrule fittings can also be flangeless, but parts and assembly differ; the name alone does not establish interchangeability.

faqItems.question: If the HSF6 model has size code 32, must the kit also be size 32?
faqItems.answer: No. The size-32 HSF6 nuts listed here cover tubing ODs of 2.0, 2.5, 3.0 and 3.2 mm, while CL-1S is selected for the actual OD. For example, 2.5 mm tubing needs CL-1S-25. Nut size group and kit tubing size are separate selections.

faqItems.question: Are CL-1S-16 and CL-1X-16 interchangeable?
faqItems.answer: No. Both accept 1.6 mm OD tubing, but CL-1S corresponds to the HSF6 M6/U28 configurations here, while CL-1X-16 pairs with HFL6-U40-16 for a 6-40 UNF connection. Check nut, port and kit geometry together.

faqItems.question: Is a dedicated assembly tool required?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Initial kit preassembly requires compatible dedicated pliers: FOREACH T-SF-4-SS, product code 959016. Hand pressure alone is unlikely to seat the ring and ferrule correctly, and higher nut torque cannot replace preassembly. Check tool compatibility with the kit and tubing size. Inspect complete, previously assembled ends before reconnecting.

faqItems.question: What torque should be used for installation?
faqItems.answer: FOREACH plastic rigid-tubing fittings with M6×1 or 1/4-28 UNF threads use 0.25–0.30 N·m; plastic U40 compression-ring fittings with 6-40 UNF threads use 0.08–0.15 N·m. These recommendations apply to threaded port tightening, not kit preassembly force.

faqItems.question: Does reconnection mean an old ring can be transferred to new tubing?
faqItems.answer: Not necessarily. Inspect sealing surfaces, ring position and tubing condition before reconnecting an intact end. Removing an old ring and installing it on another tube is a separate operation; permission depends on the specific kit requirements.

faqItems.question: Does a flush tubing end guarantee zero dead volume?
faqItems.answer: No. A square cut and correct end position help control gaps, but residual volume also depends on port geometry, tubing ID and assembly condition. Assess sample and wash lines against carryover and cleaning requirements.
